findings: Live edit response came from GBrain think fallback; trained River integration was not operational at audit time.
Health model readiness checks only API-key configuration and import of edit_component; river_client is imported lazily later and is absent in the backend interpreter.
Current source correctly derives qwen-base versus qwen-lora from actual edit_component output label; earlier source behavior is not assumed.
GBrain retrieval and existing decision readback are verified. Acceptance write code exists but this audit intentionally did not create a decision.
Ignition screen is simulated in React; UI says simulated. Accept merges browser component props and records the decision, without a live Gateway write in this app.
QM appears in README and seeded GBrain context; no executable QM integration was found in server or web code.
Accepted examples are saved to server/data/pairs.jsonl, but next_train_in is only a counter. No automatic training trigger is implemented in the accept handler.
Gray pump output alone is not proof of training, because server validation can replace green with the configured gray. Raw checkpoint output must be shown separately.
